   Does anyone want to go shopping at shopping malls any more? Not so much, thinks the owner of a Long Island mall that is replacing its traditional retail tenants with those offering activities and experiences—from an axe-throwing bar to trampolines. The mall’s occupancy has soared to 76% today from 22% in 2019. Foot traffic is growing each year. “It is definitely moving in the right direction,” said Matt Mullen, owner of Empire Adventure Park, which opened at the mall in 2024, when “there was barely a pulse in this place.” Kate King explains why the Samanea New York mall is an extreme version of an industry trend of focusing more on food and games than retail.

   Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue is back on top. It recently reclaimed its spo t as the corridor with the world’s highest retail-rent prices, surpassing previous titleholders such as London’s New Bond Street and Milan’s Via Montenapoleone. Rents on Fifth Avenue have jumped an average 35% over the past year, far outpacing 3% growth worldwide. As Kate reports, fashion houses and other retailers are once again competing to plant their flags on the most exclusive strip of the avenue.

       Hardly Anyone Shops at This Mall—and That’s Made It a Huge Success     SARA KONRADI FOR WSJ   Daniel Fishman grew up near the Samanea New York mall in this Long Island city, but he never set foot there. “I didn’t even know this mall really existed,” he said.

   Now, he’s a regular mall rat.

       Fifth Avenue Reclaims Its Crown as the World’s Premier Home to Luxury Retailers     VICTOR J. BLUE/BLOOMBERG NEWS   Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue reclaimed its spot as the corridor with the world’s highest retail-rent prices , the latest prize in the city’s accelerating real-estate recovery.

       35%   The jump in average retail-rent prices on upper Fifth Avenue over the past year, outpacing 3% growth worldwide, according to real-estate-services firm Cushman & Wakefield. Fashion houses and other retailers are once again competing to plant their flags on the most exclusive strip of the famed shopping district.

       Data Points   • 41%: The proportion of owner-occupied homes that were owned free and clear in 2025, according to Realtor.com , up from 32.8% in 2010. An aging homeowner base, all-cash purchases, refinancing into shorter loans and rising home equity have all contributed to the growing share of homeowners without mortgages.

   • 53: The Real Estate Roundtable Sentiment Index’s overall score in the fourth quarter, a 10-point drop from the third quarter. Rising interest rates and an unsettled geopolitical landscape are causing some investors to pull back, pressuring asset values, survey respondents said.

   • 20%: The increase in dollar sales for the U.S. toy industry this year through September, according to data firm Circana . Older kids and adults are driving toys’ growth, with collectible toy sales such as sports cards growing 56% year over year.

The Secret to This Mall’s Success Isn’t Shopping
 
Plus, Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue again tops worldwide rankings for highest retail rents
 
By Craig Karmin
 

This is an edition of the Real Estate newsletter, a weekly briefing of the biggest commercial deals, news, analysis and trends in office, multifamily, retail and other commercial sectors. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

Does anyone want to go shopping at shopping malls any more? Not so much, thinks the owner of a Long Island mall that is replacing its traditional retail tenants with those offering activities and experiences—from an axe-throwing bar to trampolines. The mall’s occupancy has soared to 76% today from 22% in 2019. Foot traffic is growing each year. “It is definitely moving in the right direction,” said Matt Mullen, owner of Empire Adventure Park, which opened at the mall in 2024, when “there was barely a pulse in this place.” Kate King explains why the Samanea New York mall is an extreme version of an industry trend of focusing more on food and games than retail.

 

Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue is back on top. It recently reclaimed its spot as the corridor with the world’s highest retail-rent prices, surpassing previous titleholders such as London’s New Bond Street and Milan’s Via Montenapoleone. Rents on Fifth Avenue have jumped an average 35% over the past year, far outpacing 3% growth worldwide. As Kate reports, fashion houses and other retailers are once again competing to plant their flags on the most exclusive strip of the avenue.

 
 
 

Hardly Anyone Shops at This Mall—and That’s Made It a Huge Success

 
 
SARA KONRADI FOR WSJ
 

Daniel Fishman grew up near the Samanea New York mall in this Long Island city, but he never set foot there. “I didn’t even know this mall really existed,” he said.

 

Now, he’s a regular mall rat.

 
 
 

Fifth Avenue Reclaims Its Crown as the World’s Premier Home to Luxury Retailers

 
 
VICTOR J. BLUE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue reclaimed its spot as the corridor with the world’s highest retail-rent prices, the latest prize in the city’s accelerating real-estate recovery.

 
 
 
35%
 

The jump in average retail-rent prices on upper Fifth Avenue over the past year, outpacing 3% growth worldwide, according to real-estate-services firm Cushman & Wakefield. Fashion houses and other retailers are once again competing to plant their flags on the most exclusive strip of the famed shopping district.

 
 
 

Data Points

 

• 41%: The proportion of owner-occupied homes that were owned free and clear in 2025, according to Realtor.com, up from 32.8% in 2010. An aging homeowner base, all-cash purchases, refinancing into shorter loans and rising home equity have all contributed to the growing share of homeowners without mortgages.

 

• 53: The Real Estate Roundtable Sentiment Index’s overall score in the fourth quarter, a 10-point drop from the third quarter. Rising interest rates and an unsettled geopolitical landscape are causing some investors to pull back, pressuring asset values, survey respondents said.

 

• 20%: The increase in dollar sales for the U.S. toy industry this year through September, according to data firm Circana. Older kids and adults are driving toys’ growth, with collectible toy sales such as sports cards growing 56% year over year.
